name: robotaxis
statements: b0
A Waymo robotaxi stopped in a Dallas intersection and blocked a presidential motorcade during the Republican National Convention.
b1
Waymo robotaxis had a rear-end crash rate 91% lower than human drivers.
b2
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards require manual controls such as a steering wheel and pedals in vehicles, including robotaxis.
b3
The pattern of Waymo recalls and incidents represents early warning signs of a systemic safety problem.
b4
Software defects in Waymo's autonomous driving system cause vehicles to enter freeway construction zones.
b5
Zoox will expand its paid robotaxi service from Las Vegas to additional markets after completing state regulatory requirements.
b6
It is unfair for autonomous vehicle companies to displace human rideshare drivers without providing economic protections.
b7
Policymakers should implement protections for rideshare drivers whose earnings are being reduced by the growth of robotaxi services.
b8
Waymo suspended all freeway operations in Los Angeles and Miami after a robotaxi led police on a high-speed pursuit through an active highway construction zone.
b9
NHTSA granted Zoox approval to commercially deploy up to 2,500 vehicles in each of the next two years.
Zoox cannot sell any of its robotaxi vehicles to the public as a condition of its NHTSA approval.
Uber's mass layoffs represent a strategic shift toward preparing the company for an autonomous, driverless future.
Rising competition from robotaxi operators such as Waymo is a contributing cause of Uber's decision to lay off 3,300 employees.
Waymo robotaxis will expand into additional cities beyond the 11 cities where they currently operate.
The use of Chinese-manufactured autonomous vehicles in sensitive U.S. locations poses an unacceptable national security risk.
Waymo should not expand its driverless service into Washington, D.C. until it can reliably handle presidential motorcades and sudden street closures.
Uber ceased operations in Nigeria and Uganda.
Nearly 3,900 Waymo robotaxis were recalled due to software defects related to freeway construction zones.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration granted Zoox an exemption from federal rules requiring human controls in vehicles.
Zoox's regulatory approval marks a milestone for purpose-built autonomous vehicles distinct from retrofitted conventional cars.
Flooding events caused Waymo to restrict freeway operations after vehicles entered flooded roadways.
NHTSA's investigation into Tesla's Cybercab will delay or restrict the vehicle's path to commercial deployment.
Waymo's pattern of dangerous incidents, including running red lights and entering flooded or active construction zones, represents a serious safety failure given the risk to human life.
Companies operating autonomous vehicles should proactively notify regulators and issue recalls as soon as software defects are identified, as Waymo did with its construction-zone and flooding issues.
